items.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025
items.q: I got the Sigurd Rascher book you know, Top Tones.

ctx.x: And you know I also used to play sax. I played tenor, alto, soprano, and flute. And that was one of the things – I talk about this in the book that one of the other ways that I learned about music was learning music through the instruments. You know. And I just, after I learned harmonica, and you know after about oh I don't know, three or four months of playing harmonica, that’s when I figured out how to play the chromatic scale on it which nobody had ever done on the diatonic before. And that’s a long story. But…

standard blues stuff. And then I thought well maybe I could learn some other instruments and of course Coltrane, like I said, was like a saint to me. You know. It’s like gee if I could learn how to play the saxophone, wow. That would be like a sacred instrument that I could actually learn how to play it. So someone lent me a horn and I started to learn how to play that when I was 19. And then the same thing happened with other instruments. And I was never a great saxophone player but I learned so much about the…
